item.description:
Split inbox tabs now count and list your whole inbox from the last 30 days, so a big unread backlog shows real numbers you can open and work through. The Screener and People mode are gone: new senders land in Important or Other again. The account switcher on Mac and the account menu on iPhone show each account's photo, the Lock Screen's inline Next Meeting widget fits events on other days again, and tapping Today twice in the iPhone's 3-day view no longer makes the grid jump. There's also a new experiment in Settings → Flags: Tasks, a third mode that keeps a plain-text todo list with reminders and a task from any email.

  • The iPhone Lock Screen's inline Next Meeting widget fits an event on another day again
  • The iPhone account menu shows each account's photo
  • The Mac account switcher's All accounts icon shows the accounts' photos
  • The Screener and People mode are gone
  • Split inbox tab counts and lists now cover the whole inbox from the last 30 days instead of only the first 40 threads
  • Tapping Today twice in the iPhone's 3-day view no longer makes the grid jump back and forth
  • Tasks mode behind Settings → Flags → Tasks

Pictures that travel inside an email now show where the sender put them, on Mac and iPhone: signature logos, pasted screenshots and the scans of your mail in USPS Informed Delivery used to appear as an Inline image placeholder. They load even with remote images off, since nothing leaves the message, and an image shown in the body no longer repeats as an attachment.

  • Inline images now show on Mac and iPhone

Two bigger pieces, both easy to switch off. A daily brief greets you the first time you open the Smart tab each day: what needs a reply, what you're waiting on, follow-ups due, today's meetings with a countdown to the first, and chips for new senders and conversations to reply later; close it for the day, bring it back with ⇧T or from the menu bar, and there's an optional morning notification under Settings → Mail. People is a new experimental mode, off by default under Settings → Flags: everyone you actually talk to, with last-talked dates, your history of conversations and meetings with each person, and keep-in-touch reminders that also show up in the brief.

  • A daily brief gathers the day in one place
  • People is a third mode beside Mail and Calendar (⌘3)
  • Settings gains a Flags pane for experimental features, and People now ships behind its flag, off by default

Five bigger changes this time, all of them reversible from Settings if you don't want them. An empty inbox is now a proper moment: the headline follows the time of day and the rest of today's calendar sits underneath it. The calendar's Today, arrows and Day/Week/Month controls float in a glass capsule over the grid, and the ⌘K palette is glass too (Appearance → Glass controls turns it off). An event's card briefs you before a meeting with when you last met the person and your recent conversations with the guests. Mail gains a Screener tab that holds first-time senders until you press y to allow or n to screen them out (Mail → Screener turns it off), and a Reply Later tray on l. And mail meets calendar: drag a conversation onto the agenda rail or the week grid to block time for it, and press S in the calendar to draw availability slots you can copy or insert into a reply.

  • Releases no longer fail when notarytool submit itself crashes
  • An empty inbox is now a designed moment instead of a generic placeholder
  • The calendar's Today, previous/next and Day/Week/Month controls now float in a Liquid Glass capsule over the bottom of the grid, Fantastical-style, and the ⌘K palette card is glass too, so the header gets shorter and content shows through the controls while labels stay legible over busy afternoons (the capsule is tinted toward the surface color, the grid and month view reserve room under it so the now line and late events never hide beneath it, and keyboard shortcuts are unchanged); Settings → Appearance → Glass controls turns it off and restores the matte header and palette exactly as before
  • An event's detail card now briefs you before the meeting
  • Mail gains a Screener and a Reply Later tray, both local-only with no Gmail writes
  • Mail and calendar now meet in two places
  • The iPhone app builds again and shows the new Screener tab with its waiting count, so conversations the Mac's Screener is holding are still reachable on the phone instead of disappearing from every inbox tab

Summaries stay put when you quit and reopen Meridian: a thread from someone in your contacts no longer gets its summary written all over again, and an open thread no longer sits on Summarizing… after the app finishes starting up.

  • A thread's summary survives quitting and reopening instead of being written again or sitting on Summarizing…

Meridian holds still: opening a thread, switching folders, refreshing and moving through mail no longer flash, jump or blink, and the calendar stops refetching and re-raising errors when one calendar fails. Summaries are written in the background when mail arrives, so a thread opens with its summary ready, and the mail agenda opens on its own only when the email has a date in it. iCloud Mail accounts (icloud.com, me.com, mac.com) can now be added alongside Gmail, with step-by-step help for making the app-specific password Apple requires. Settings fits on screen, picking an accent color repaints in place, sign-in, push and link handling are tighter, and invites for meetings that have already started leave To respond. On iPhone you can move a conversation to Trash, switching inbox tabs no longer slides rows around, the time grid ends cleanly at midnight, swiping between days no longer jumps, and the Lock Screen's inline widget opens the event.

You can now attach files to mail: use the paperclip or drag files in on the Mac, or pick from Photos or Files on iPhone. A reply that's still waiting to send has its own Undo button, and replying to an unread thread marks it read once the reply goes out. Your own avatar now uses your own contact photo, the selected thread stays highlighted when the list re-sorts, quoted history in reply chains that include a calendar invite collapses again, and Outlook mail no longer shows faint grey text on a white box in dark mode.

  • Your own account's avatar uses your own contact card's photo
  • Attach files to mail
  • The selected thread is highlighted when the list re-sorts as you open it
  • Note for the next session
  • A reply chain that quotes a Google invite collapses its quoted history again
  • A reply waiting out its undo window can be taken back from its dimmed card in the reader
  • Replying to an unread thread marks it read once the reply is sent
  • Outlook mail no longer shows faint grey text on a white box in dark mode

Tapping a new-mail notification from another account now switches Meridian to that account, so the inbox and the open email match instead of showing one account's list beside another's message.

  • Opening a new-mail notification for another account switches to that account

Calendar event popovers open cleanly instead of jumping in size as they appear. The window drags from its header bars again, not just the thin strip at the top. The account switcher is tidier and closes as soon as you pick an account, without the whole window springing.

  • The window drags from its header bars again
  • The account switcher looks tidier and gets out of the way faster
  • Calendar event popovers open without jumping in size

Archiving, typing and the command palette are smoother, with less stalling when you clear mail quickly. New-mail notifications have an Archive button, so you can clear a message without opening the app. The Snoozed folder shows your snoozed conversations again, soonest first. Copy message link opens in the right Google account, and summaries skip plain invites, receipts and notices and focus on the latest state of a thread.

  • Archiving, typing and the command palette stop stalling the main thread
  • Summaries skip mail that says what it is in its subject and read small-model threads from the newest end
  • Perf tooling for layout work
  • Layout research write-up
  • The Snoozed folder lists your snoozed threads again on Gmail accounts
  • New-mail notifications get an Archive button on Mac and iPhone

A cancelled event no longer sends you its reminder on iPhone. Replies and forwards now show in the conversation as soon as you press Send, and forwards stay in the thread you forwarded from, as they do in Gmail. Going back to an email no longer makes it jump, the cursor in recipient fields lines up with the names beside it, and replies to invites are logged so problems can be traced.

  • Release notes list every commit since the last release
  • Invite replies and error toasts are logged so a reply that doesn't stick can be traced
  • The caret in a recipient field lines up with the chips beside it
  • Going back to an email no longer makes it jump
  • A reply shows in its thread the moment you press Send, dimmed while the undo window runs and while it sends, then the sent message takes its place without anything moving
  • Plan for the archive (e) delay
  • A forward stays in the conversation you forwarded from, like Gmail web
  • A cancelled event no longer sends its reminder on iPhone
When you accept a recurring invitation for all events, every occurrence on screen shows your answer right away, instead of only the one you clicked.
No visible changes in this release: it moves how Meridian is built, signed and published to a new setup, so future updates can ship from any of our Macs.

Events in the week view can be dragged again, including a new event while its editor is open: the editor steps aside and comes back beside the moved event with what you typed. The thread you have selected keeps its Smart lane until you move off it, and a thread you archived no longer comes back after a refresh.

Meeting reminders are on by default, and Meridian asks for notification permission at launch so they arrive without finding the setting. Settings shows whether each account gets server notifications, with Set Up… to connect one. An invite you answer stays where it is in the list until you move on, instead of jumping away under you.

New mail summaries are ready when you open a thread instead of loading. Recipient suggestions put your own addresses you've written to first. Checked threads that leave the list are unchecked. Notifications never show a generic "New mail" placeholder. A notification's own timestamp no longer offers Add to calendar, and "tomorrow 4:30–5pm" proposes a 30-minute slot.

The menu bar shows the next event all day, not just within 4 hours. ` cycles the inbox tabs (⇧` goes back). Settings shows whether links can open in each account's Chrome profile, with an Allow… button when macOS blocks it.

Suggested events now cover multi-day ranges: an offsite on Oct 20–22, a Thursday-through-Sunday trip or a hotel stay becomes one event across those days, and a meeting proposed inside a trip, a narrowed day or a cancellation wins over the range. The month view draws multi-day events as one bar, X multi-selects threads like Gmail, agenda rail events open their details, summaries no longer offer to add an event an invite already covers, calendar write prompts are no longer hidden behind the event popover, and images load by default.

Event alerts follow your Google Calendar notification settings on Mac and iPhone. The agenda rail now finds the meeting a thread is actually arranging: confirmed times take their day from earlier proposals, declines and cancellations are respected, and time zones and casual times like 530pm are understood.
Images in mail now load on iPhone: the Mac shares its private image proxy with your other devices over iCloud.
iPhone calendar improvements ship alongside: multi-day events span their days, pinch to change the range, drag to create.
Superhuman replies now collapse their quoted history. New accounts learn from the last 30 days of mail without filling To respond with old threads.
Expanding a message no longer makes the thread jump when scroll bars are set to always show.
Apple Intelligence now summarizes emails it used to refuse as sensitive. Calendar invites you've already answered no longer sit in To respond. The reply composer's recipients line up with its header.
Apple Intelligence summaries now finish even if you move to another email before they're ready, instead of falling back to a basic summary.
Click a date in a summary to see that day in the agenda, and add the event right from the sidebar without leaving Mail. The selected email stays highlighted after archiving the one below it.
Replies are written right in the thread, like Gmail: the reply box sits under the last message, matches its width and style, and scrolls into view when you open it.
Open an event's invite email from its ⋯ menu. Settings and onboarding show whether notifications are allowed and help turn them on. Clicking a new-mail notification keeps that thread open.
Opening an earlier message in a conversation now slides the rest down smoothly instead of hopping.
Moving through mail with J/K is snappier: the selection highlight appears immediately and the conversation follows a frame later.
Mail's agenda rail now jumps to the day an email proposes — "can you do Sunday?" shows your Sunday, with the proposed time marked.
Attachments: click any attachment to preview it in Quick Look, or right-click to open or save it. iPhone builds can now compose, reply and forward.

Meeting joins, calendar links and links in emails now open in the Chrome profile signed into that account (personal meetings open in your personal profile). Fixes a crash when cancelling Google sign-in while adding an account.
Under the hood: Meridian now builds in Swift 6 with complete data-race checking, and shared state that background work touches is lock-protected by the compiler.
Mail settings no longer overlap; Esc closes Settings; Private Cloud Compute shows as unavailable when this build isn't enabled for it
To respond errs on the side of telling you: review and signature requests, assignments and comment questions now show up.
Settings: recent calendar changes moved to a scrollable Activity tab, so Add Google account is always visible on the Accounts tab.
Much more accurate To respond: receipts, notices, newsletters and cold pitches stay out; forwards from teammates show up.
A larger, easier-to-read event editor with aligned rows.
Fixes a one-second freeze when scrolling the inbox and at launch; faster startup.
Inbox labels load instantly from the mail cache. On iPhone, app data now stays private to the app (only the widget and notification files are shared); you may need to sign in again.
Faster summaries after relaunch: AI results are kept with each account's mail cache and refreshed only when a thread actually changes. Clear cache and sign-out remove them too.
Apple Intelligence summaries and triage actually run again (they were stuck on Basic). Basic summaries no longer repeat the email or ask about events that are over.
Better Apple Intelligence summaries: dates come from the email itself, no filler bullets or copied examples, and summaries no longer get stuck on Basic at launch. The AI draft reply is gone.
Bcc: compose with Bcc, and see who you Bcc'd on your sent mail
The send toast now reads "Sent · Undo" (no countdown); the Undo goes when the window ends. Toasts no longer truncate Undo. To/Cc suggestions include your own addresses.
Browsing mail no longer marks threads read: j/k, arrows, clicks and archive only preview. Return, o or double-click opens a thread and marks it read.

Mail is marked read only when you open a thread (Return, o or double-click); browsing the list just previews. While a thread is open, arrows and space scroll it, n/p step through its messages, and the list highlight turns grey. Fixes: a newer toast no longer takes away a pending send's Undo, and each Undo button undoes its own action.

Fixes for mail and calendar edge cases: Reply honours Reply-To and never answers your own drafts; deleting one message no longer makes a whole thread look trashed; a failing calendar keeps its events; moving a repeating series to another day moves every occurrence; guests' notes and plus-ones survive edits; Google Calendar descriptions show as plain text; better handling of attached messages, inline attachments, international charsets and format=flowed mail.

Live calendar updates: your calendar refreshes the moment it changes elsewhere (with instant notifications on). Invitations whose event was deleted now say so and no longer offer Accept / Maybe / Decline, and invite cards re-check with Google when you open the email.

Full Gmail and Calendar access at sign-in (no more Enable editing); clicking away from the event editor discards unsaved changes; security fixes: calendar writes need the calendar grant, sends only from the account shown in From, one allowed-permission set on Mac and iPhone; plus fixes from the second-model review.

Identity from Google only (colleague calendars are read-only, RSVPs only as you); safer sends (no double sends, may-have-sent checked by send id and Gmail history); snooze, invite card and recurring-event fixes; calendar disk cache and refresh; faster launch and triage; a sign-in welcome screen instead of sample data.
First public release: a notarized download for Mac, with automatic updates.
